# Front-end data format

The front end reads one file: `evidence/frontend_data.json`. Regenerate it after any eval with:

```bash
uv run python -m spendradar export
```

Every value is copied from a scorecard (`evidence/evals/*.json`), a run's state (`runs/<id>/state.json`, local only) or a ground-truth file. The front end should display these values, not recompute them. All company finance data is fictional; competitors are real companies with data from Crustdata.

## Top level

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | int | Bumped when a field changes meaning. Currently `1`. |
| `generated_at` | ISO datetime | When the export ran. |
| `companies` | Company[] | Acme first (the development set), then held-out companies A–Z. |
| `business` | object | Paths to the cfo.ai plan (`plan`), unit costs (`unit_costs`) and the cfo.ai exports folder (`cfoai_exports`). |

## Company

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | Folder name under `data/`, e.g. `ledgerly`. |
| `name` | string | e.g. `Ledgerly Payments Inc.` |
| `industry` | string | e.g. `fintech (spend management)` |
| `role` | `"development"` \| `"held_out"` | Acme is the company the agent was built against. Held-out companies were never used to tune it. |
| `fictional` | bool | Always `true`; show a "fictional data" label. |
| `competitors` | {name, domain}[] | Real peers the agent compares against. |
| `negative_controls` | string[] | Planted items the agent must NOT flag (e.g. a 0.4% rounding difference). A flag on one counts as a false alarm. |
| `runs` | Run[] | Oldest first. The last one is the current state. |

## Run

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | string | e.g. `1010-d514dc` |
| `variant` | string | Label for what was being tested, e.g. `baseline-kestrel`, `after-heldout-fixes-kestrel`. Use it to pair before/after. |
| `scored_at` | ISO datetime | When the scorecard was written. |
| `git_sha` | string | Commit the run used. A `-dirty` suffix means uncommitted changes were present. |
| `neatlogs_trace_id` | string | Searchable in the neatlogs dashboard (app.neatlogs.com). |
| `scorecard` | path | The JSON this run was copied from. |
| `data_mode` | `"real"` \| `"fixture"` | `fixture` = altered competitor data, eval only. Must be shown prominently. |
| `injected_faults` | string[] | Faults deliberately injected (e.g. `crustdata:429`); empty for normal runs. |
| `metrics` | object | See below. |
| `planted` | {id, label, caught}[] | Each planted error and whether this run caught it. Good for a ✓/✗ grid. |
| `false_alarm_detail` | string[] | What the agent flagged that the ground truth says is fine. |
| `report` | {markdown, html, available_locally} | Paths to the run's full report. `runs/` is not committed, so `available_locally` is false on other machines. |
| `findings` | Finding[] | Empty unless the run's state is available locally. |

Written for: you, as input to the front-end design doc.

## What the front end is for

It makes the agent's work visible to the judges in one place, and gives the 3-minute video something clean to film. The two judging categories it supports most are "the agent" (30%) and "the demo video" (20%) [proof: CLAUDE.md §1]. It should show four things judges can't easily see from the code:

1. **It works on companies it was never tuned on.** There are 7 fictional companies across 6 industries, and the latest run of each catches all its planted errors [proof: frontend_data.json]. The exception is Acme's latest run, at 4/5; that's the audit bug I just fixed, and the 3 new runs will replace it.
2. **It catches its own mistakes.** Self-audit findings that ended up `downgraded` or `overturned`, with the auditor's reasoning.
3. **It recovers from failures.** The recovery decisions, especially those where the LLM chose differently from the fixed rule. There are 166 of those across the runs [proof: export count, sum of the "non-default-recovery" column].
4. **Every number has a source.** Each run shows its neatlogs trace ID, commit hash and scorecard file.

## Hard rules the design must respect

- **Static site, one data file.** It reads `evidence/frontend_data.json` and nothing else. No backend and no live LLM calls, because of CLAUDE.md rule 9, zero spend.
- **Show numbers, never compute new ones.** Every number on screen comes from the file [proof: docs/frontend-data.md "display these values, not recompute them"], because CLAUDE.md rule 7 forbids fabricated numbers.
- **Visible labels:**
  - a "fictional company data" label on every company page (`fictional: true`);
  - `data_mode` (REAL or FIXTURE), shown prominently;
  - an "injected fault" badge when `injected_faults` isn't empty.

## Screens, in priority order

| # | Screen | What it shows (fields) | Used in video |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Overview / generalisation table** | One row per company: name, industry, development or held-out, first run vs latest run (`planted_caught/planted_total`, `false_alarms`) | Opening shot (0:00–0:40) |
| 2 | **Run detail** | Metric tiles (LLM calls, tokens, latency, fallback hops, Crustdata credits); a ✓/✗ grid of planted errors; findings grouped by status, each with its `confidence`; the neatlogs trace ID | Result section (2:20–2:50) |
| 3 | **"The agent disproved itself"** | Findings with status `overturned` or `downgraded`, with `audit_notes` showing both sides, including the second opinion | Opening hook (0:00–0:15) |
| 4 | **Recovery log** | `task_id`, `chosen`, `rule_default`, `reason`, with rows where `chosen ≠ rule_default` highlighted; failure-injection runs badged | neatlogs section (0:40–1:20) |
| 5 | **Before / after** | Runs paired by `variant` (e.g. `baseline-kestrel` → `after-heldout-fixes-kestrel`) | Bug-fix story |
| 6 | **Business** | Links to the cfo.ai plan, plus a few headline figures | cfo.ai section (1:45–2:20) |

Screen 6's numbers aren't in the data file [proof: docs/frontend-data.md "Suggested views" item 4], so I'd add them to the export.

The video timings are from [evidence/demo-script.md](evidence/demo-script.md) and CLAUDE.md §13.

## Gaps I'd close in the export once your design is ready

- **Findings and recovery logs exist for only 28 of the 45 runs.** Older Acme runs' folders aren't on this laptop, so their findings and recovery lists are empty [proof: export count]. The held-out companies are complete.
- **Report text isn't included.** `runs/` isn't committed, so `report.available_locally` is false anywhere except the laptop that made the runs [proof: docs/frontend-data.md]. If you want a report view, I'll put the report text into the JSON.
- **No step-by-step timeline.** An "agent loop" view (plan → act → verify → recover → audit, step by step) would need the per-step history added to the export. It's the most cinematic view for the video, but it's extra work. Say whether you want it.
- **Business numbers:** as above, for screen 6.

## What the design doc needs to decide

1. **Look and feel:** colours, type, light or dark mode. Recording the video favours one strong theme.
2. **Hosting:** a link judges can open, e.g. GitHub Pages {unverified}, or only local for the video.
3. **Framework:** a plain HTML page is simplest. Say if you'd prefer React or something else.
4. **Which of screens 1–6 to keep** if time runs short. I'd keep 1, 3 and 4 at minimum.
5. **Whether to include the agent-loop timeline** from the gaps above.

Skip any login, settings, input forms or "run the agent" button. It can't run for free from a browser, and the judges don't need it.

I can save this brief as `docs/frontend-brief.md` in the repo so Akarsh sees it too. The Acme runs are still going; I'll report and push when they finish.
